title: The rusting nail experiment in three test tubes
examples: What does iron need to rust?
Why is the water boiled in the rusting experiment?

explain.say: Here is a real experiment you might do at school. Three iron nails, three test tubes, and one question: what does iron need to rust? Look at the board. Each tube tests something different.

draw.text: The rusting nail experiment in three test tubes

explain.say: See tube 1? The nail sits in ordinary water, open to the air. After a week, it is covered in orange-brown rust. So water plus air causes rust. But is it the water, the air, or both? What do you think?

Look at tube 2. The water was boiled to drive out the air, and a layer of oil on top stops new air getting in. No air means no oxygen, and the nail stays shiny! So what do you think iron needs from the air?

Oxygen! Now look at tube 3. It has air, but a drying agent called calcium chloride soaks up all the water vapour. No water, and again no rust. So iron needs both water and oxygen. Do you think salt would speed it up?

Yes, salt makes rust faster! Great experimenting, you think like a scientist. Look at the reasons on the board: steel coated in zinc, called galvanised, is protected even if scratched, because zinc reacts first. Wow: ships carry zinc blocks on their hulls that slowly corrode to save the steel.

faq.q: What does iron need to rust?
faq.a: Iron needs both water and oxygen. In the experiment, the nail rusts only in the tube that has both.

faq.q: Why is the water boiled in tube 2?
faq.a: Boiling drives out the dissolved air, so there is no oxygen in the water. The oil layer stops air dissolving back in.
asks: Why put oil on the water?

faq.q: What does calcium chloride do in tube 3?
faq.a: Calcium chloride is a drying agent. It absorbs water vapour from the air, so the nail is kept completely dry.
asks: What is the drying agent for?

faq.a: A more reactive metal, like zinc or magnesium, is attached to iron. It corrodes instead of the iron, protecting it, even where the coating is scratched.

faq.q: What is the word equation for rusting?
faq.a: Iron plus oxygen plus water gives hydrated iron(III) oxide, which is rust.

facts: Iron rusts only when both oxygen and water are present.

quiz.say: A nail is kept in a sealed tube of dry air with calcium chloride. What happens after a week?
quiz.show: A nail is kept in a sealed tube of dry air with calcium chloride. What happens after a week?
quiz.why: There is oxygen but no water, so it cannot rust.

wrong.0: Time of day makes no difference; water is missing.
